# AMD Instinct vLLM serving validation campaign (go/no-go)

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's core unknown: whether vLLM serving on AMD Instinct accelerators (ROCm) achieves functional and performance parity with the platform's productized CUDA builds for the supported model set. It executes a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware and produces the go/no-go report that determines which models the ROCm serving runtime productization will cover. It also covers securing access to the dedicated AMD Instinct nodes the campaign requires (procurement or partner-lab access — the mechanism is unresolved in the strategy).

## Scope

- Secure dedicated AMD Instinct nodes for the campaign (via procurement or partner-lab access)
- Define the parity methodology: per-model functional correctness criteria and the performance baseline (throughput and latency) against the CUDA builds on comparable hardware
- Run functional validation: vLLM ROCm serving for each model in the supported model set
- Run performance measurement: throughput and latency per model against the CUDA baseline
- Produce the go/no-go report: per-model pass/fail results, supporting parity data, and the recommended productization scope for the models that clear

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dedicated AMD Instinct nodes are available to the campaign (procured or accessed via partner lab)
- Every model in the agreed supported model set has a recorded functional pass/fail result for vLLM ROCm serving against the defined correctness criteria
- Every model in the set has recorded performance measurements (throughput and latency) against the CUDA baseline
- A go/no-go report is delivered listing cleared and failed models with supporting data and a recommended productization scope

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishing functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization — fully covered by this epic

## Risks and Notes

- Hardware access (procurement vs partner lab) is unresolved and externally controlled; it gates the start of the campaign but does not change what the campaign does.
- Upstream ROCm runtime image availability for the campaign's vLLM builds is controlled by AMD and upstream communities.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

This epic productizes a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models cleared by the validation campaign's go/no-go scope, alongside the existing CUDA runtime builds. It builds and releases the ROCm runtime image per platform version and makes the runtime deployable through KServe InferenceServices via the ServingRuntime CRD. KServe itself requires no code change (runtimes plug in through the ServingRuntime CRD), so KServe compatibility is validated as part of this epic rather than as separate serving-stack work.

## Scope

- Supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime (ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime) covering the models cleared by the validation campaign
- ROCm runtime image build and release through the standard serving runtime release pipeline, pinned to an upstream ROCm release compatible with the platform release train
- Validation that the runtime deploys and serves through KServe InferenceServices (passive KServe coverage — no KServe code changes)
- Confirmation that existing CUDA (NVIDIA) runtime builds and their serving behavior are unaffected

## Acceptance Criteria

- A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is available for every model in the validation campaign's cleared (go/no-go) scope
- The ROCm runtime image builds and is released through the standard serving runtime release pipeline for the target platform version
- The runtime deploys via a ServingRuntime and serves requests through a KServe InferenceService for the cleared models
- Existing CUDA (NVIDIA) runtime builds and their serving behavior are unaffected
- The runtime image is pinned to an upstream ROCm release compatible with the target platform release train

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears — fully covered by this epic
- Passive-component coverage: KServe (validation only, no code change) is covered by the KServe InferenceService compatibility acceptance criteria above

## Risks and Notes

- Upstream ROCm image release cadence is controlled by AMD and upstream communities and may not align with platform release trains; version pinning must be validated against the target train.
- The runtime's supported-model scope is defined by the validation campaign outcome: fewer cleared models means a narrower scope; if no models clear, this productization is descoped.

# PyTorch ROCm training support for PyTorchJobs

## Description

This epic enables PyTorch training on AMD Instinct (ROCm) accelerators for jobs run through the Training Operator: single-GPU and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs execute on AMD GPU nodes using ROCm builds of the PyTorch training images, alongside the existing NVIDIA-based training support. ## Scope

- PyTorchJob support on ROCm: single-GPU and multi-GPU jobs using supported PyTorch ROCm training images
- Job pods request `amd.com/gpu` resources and are schedulable on AMD Instinct nodes
- Verification that multi-GPU PyTorchJobs run to completion on AMD Instinct nodes
- Confirmation that existing NVIDIA-based PyTorchJob training is unaffected

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob using a PyTorch ROCm training image runs to completion on an AMD Instinct node
- A multi-GPU PyTorchJob runs to completion across multiple AMD GPUs on Instinct nodes
- Job worker pods request `amd.com/gpu` resources consistent with AMD accelerator nodes
- Existing NVIDIA-based PyTorchJob training behavior is unaffected

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs — the job-execution half of this requirement is covered by this epic; the Kueue admission and `amd.com/gpu` quota half is covered by the companion quota-handling work

## Risks and Notes

- Final on-hardware validation requires access to AMD Instinct nodes; code and image work can proceed in advance.
- AMD GPU node infrastructure (drivers, accelerator discovery exposing `amd.com/gpu`) is assumed to be provided with the AMD nodes — it is not in the platform inventory today.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for ROCm workloads

## Description

This epic enables Kueue admission and quota accounting for AMD GPUs (`amd.com/gpu`) so that ROCm training jobs (such as PyTorchJobs) are admitted through the platform's queueing system with correct quota handling, alongside existing NVIDIA GPU quota support. It covers the queueing/orchestration half of ROCm training support; the PyTorchJob-on-ROCm execution itself is covered by the Training Operator work within the same team.

## Scope

- Quota configuration for the `amd.com/gpu` resource: ClusterQueue/LocalQueue resource flavors covering AMD Instinct nodes
- Admission of ROCm training jobs through Kueue with all-or-nothing (gang) semantics and correct `amd.com/gpu` quota accounting
- Coverage of `amd.com/gpu` in Kueue's quota usage metrics where NVIDIA GPUs are covered today
- Confirmation that existing NVIDIA GPU quota handling is unaffected

## Acceptance Criteria

- A ClusterQueue/LocalQueue configuration admits workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu` with correct quota accounting
- A multi-GPU ROCm training job is admitted through Kueue only when quota and AMD GPU capacity are available (all-or-nothing admission)
- `amd.com/gpu` quota usage is observable through Kueue's exposed metrics
- Existing NVIDIA GPU quota handling is unaffected

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): jobs admitted through Kueue with `amd.com/gpu` quota handling — the admission/quota half of this requirement is covered by this epic; the single-/multi-GPU PyTorch ROCm training half is covered by the Training Operator work

## Risks and Notes

- End-to-end admission validation of ROCm jobs benefits from coordination with the PyTorch ROCm training work in the same team (shared validation cluster), but the two efforts have no build-against dependency and proceed in parallel.
- Final on-hardware validation requires access to AMD Instinct nodes.

# Konflux onboarding for the vLLM ROCm runtime image

## Description

This epic onboards the new vLLM ROCm runtime container image build in the existing midstream repository (opendatahub-io/vllm) to Konflux. The repository is already Konflux-onboarded for its existing CUDA (NVIDIA) image builds; the ROCm runtime is a new container image in that repository and needs its own build pipeline configuration. The onboarding runs in parallel with the ROCm serving runtime productization work — there is deliberately no blocking edge in either direction: the coupling is enforced by the build-pipeline acceptance criterion on the productization work, never by a DAG dependency.

## Scope

- Konflux build pipeline configuration for the vLLM ROCm runtime container image in the midstream repository
- Build recipe following the repository's existing Konflux onboarding patterns for the CUDA image builds
- Verification build proving the new pipeline builds the ROCm image from midstream source

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Konflux build pipeline is configured for the vLLM ROCm runtime container image in the midstream repository
- The Konflux build pipeline for the ROCm image completes with a green build from midstream source
- The pipeline configuration follows the repository's existing Konflux recipes for the CUDA image builds

## HLR Traceability

- Enabling epic for HLR-2 (P0): provides the Konflux build pipeline for the ROCm vLLM runtime image that the serving runtime productization builds and releases through; no direct HLR coverage of its own

## Risks and Notes

- Deliberately parallel to the ROCm serving runtime productization work (pipeline configuration is independent of runtime code): the coupling is the build-pipeline acceptance criterion on that epic, not a DAG dependency. Serializing the two would mis-serialize parallel work.
- The upstream ROCm base image version compatibility decided by the productization work is filled in at execution time; it does not change the pipeline configuration approach.
